assumptions: 'Success rate' means attempt-level success rate: successful attempts divided by all attempts, with each retry counted as a separate attempt. Order-level and technical rates are shown alongside.
The comparison is 25–31 Oct 2026 versus 18–24 Oct 2026, the immediately preceding period of equal length, since no period was specified.
caveats: Attempt volume was about 39% above the usual level for these weekdays across 18–31 Oct. This could reflect a sale or a data gap; it is not an error by itself, but check before comparing totals across this period.
Success rate depends on the denominator: attempt-level is 88.5%, order-level is 90.7% and technical is 92.0%. Retries and customer drop-offs explain the gap.
Failure codes are quoted per 100 attempts for Harbor Bank debit cards only, so they describe that segment, not the whole business.

facts.text: Attempt success rate fell 0.18pp from 88.6% (102,154 of 115,254 attempts) to 88.5% (101,587 of 114,846 attempts). The p-value is 0.178, so the change is neither statistically nor practically significant.
Payment-method mix explains essentially none of the change: the mix effect is about 0.00pp and the rate (like-for-like) effect is -0.18pp.
Debit card is 16.4% of volume but accounts for -0.23pp of the change; its own success rate fell from 84.0% to 82.7%. Other payment methods moved by 0.06pp or less in either direction.
Within debit cards, Harbor Bank is where the drop is concentrated: its debit-card success rate fell 3.89pp from 78.6% to 74.7%, contributing -0.16pp to the overall change (q-value 0.00069).

For Harbor Bank debit cards, ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE rose from 8.42 to 13.86 failures per 100 attempts (+5.44), the largest shift. 3DS abandonment, DO_NOT_HONOR and invalid CVV each fell, partly offsetting it.
Harbor Bank debit daily success rate sat at 83.7%–86.3% on 18–20 Oct, then dropped to 73.3% on 21 Oct and stayed around 72.6%–75.2% through 29 Oct.
Other dimensions show no meaningful movement: merchant group, channel, region and merchant tier have like-for-like effects that are small or offsetting (for example NovaMart +0.14pp).

response.headline: Success rate barely moved: it fell 0.18pp from 88.6% to 88.5%, which is not statistically significant. Payment-method mix did not change; the small dip is a like-for-like rate drop concentrated in Harbor Bank debit cards.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Ask Harbor Bank or the acquirer whether risk or fraud rules changed around 21 Oct, and check whether declines cluster on specific amounts, merchants or BIN ranges.
hypotheses.rationale: The step change on 21 Oct is sharp and sustained, and the increase is almost entirely in ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE, an issuer-side risk code, while technical and customer-drop-off codes did not rise.
hypotheses.text: Harbor Bank tightened its risk rules for debit cards around 21 Oct, causing more risk declines.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Harbor Bank tightened its risk rules for debit cards around 21 Oct, causing more risk declines.
recommendations.rationale: This single segment accounts for most of the overall dip, and the shift started on one specific date.
recommendations.text: Raise the Harbor Bank debit-card risk-decline increase with the issuer through the acquirer and ask for the rule change and any whitelisting options.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: For Harbor Bank debit cards, ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE rose from 8.42 to 13.86 failures per 100 attempts (+5.44), the largest shift.
recommendations.rationale: Pinpointing the affected traffic helps target a fix and confirms whether the shift persists.
recommendations.text: Break down Harbor Bank debit risk declines by merchant, ticket size and BIN to see whether specific traffic is being blocked, and monitor this segment daily.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Attempt success rate fell 0.18pp from 88.6% to 88.5%; the p-value is 0.178, so the change is not significant.
recommendations.rationale: The overall change is within normal statistical noise.
recommendations.text: Do not treat the overall 0.18pp dip as an incident on its own; track it for another week before escalating broadly.
